comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C6 regarding Lin A/15 lineage characterization. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED as established background, with OpenEval citing specific references (Baek and Mann 2009; Brierley et al. 2012; Enriquez et al. 2018) and peer reviewers acknowledging this as solid foundational evidence.

Perfect agreement on claims C7-C12 regarding temporal patterns of apoptosis during larval stages. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with OpenEval highlighting immunostaining evidence and peer reviewers noting 'solid evidence' for temporal windows and cell death patterns.

Perfect agreement on claims C13-C21 regarding neuroblast decommissioning timing and PCD mechanism. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with OpenEval emphasizing quantification and P35 rescue experiments, while peer reviewers accept findings about neuroblast lifespan control.

Perfect agreement on claims C22-C29 regarding Imp/Syp temporal expression and functional role in NB decommissioning. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED as central contributions, with OpenEval noting smFISH and immunostaining data, and peer reviewers explicitly acknowledging these as key findings.

Perfect agreement on claims C30-C38 regarding selective elimination of late-born neurons. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with OpenEval highlighting EdU labeling and quantitative data, while peer reviewers note evidence shows 'only the last-born neurons are precisely and progressively eliminated through PCD.'

Partial agreement on claims C39-C42 (opposite gradients of Imp/Syp). OpenEval R6 covers C39-C42 while peer R6 covers C39-C50, extending to functional experiments. Both find claims SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers emphasizing cell-autonomous function in post-mitotic neurons.

Strong agreement on claims C43-C50 regarding genetic manipulation experiments. OpenEval R7 and peer R6 both cover these claims and find them SUPPORTED, with OpenEval highlighting MARCM experiments and peer reviewers noting that 'Imp promotes survival, whereas Syp promotes cell death.'

Perfect agreement on claims C51-C60 regarding transcription factor codes and neuronal fate. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with OpenEval noting PCCD computational analysis and peer reviewers linking 'fate of neuronal survival with its specification.'

Perfect agreement on claims C61-C65 regarding sufficiency of TF code changes for survival. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with OpenEval highlighting MARCM quantification and peer reviewers noting that 'mis-expression of early-born transcription factors in later-born cells can be sufficient to block apoptosis.'

Partial agreement on claims C66-C68. OpenEval R10 covers C66-C68 while peer R9 covers C66, C68, and C78-C82. Both find claims SUPPORTED as integrative conclusions, with peer reviewers emphasizing the 'intriguing demonstration of how the nervous system is constructed.'

Minimal overlap on claim C67 only. OpenEval R10 includes C67 among C66-C68, while peer R10 includes C67 among C67-C77. Both find claims SUPPORTED as established background knowledge from prior studies.

Partial agreement on claims C78-C82 (integrative mechanistic conclusions). OpenEval R11 covers C69-C82 while peer R9 covers C66, C68, C78-C82. Both find claims SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers noting the study 'demonstrate that the differential expression of Imp and Syp in iMNs links precise neuronal generation and distinct identities.'

Strong agreement on claims C69-C77 regarding established Imp/Syp roles. OpenEval R11 covers C69-C82 while peer R10 covers C67-C77. Both find claims SUPPORTED as background knowledge, with peer reviewers noting 'mutually antagonistic roles for Imp and Syp during nervous system development.'

Partial agreement on claims C83-C84. OpenEval finds C83 SUPPORTED but C84 UNCERTAIN (labeled as hypothesis), resulting in overall UNCERTAIN evaluation. Peer R11 covers C83-C97 and finds all SUPPORTED as background/implications. OpenEval is more cautious about the speculative evolutionary hypothesis in C84.

Strong agreement on claims C85-C97 regarding established background on Imp/Syp conservation and biomedical relevance. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED as prior knowledge providing context, with peer reviewers acknowledging evolutionary conservation and broader implications.

Perfect agreement on claims C98-C118 regarding established background on Drosophila neurogenesis. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED as foundational knowledge, with OpenEval noting extensive citations and peer reviewers treating this as accurate context for new findings.

Perfect agreement on claims C119-C128 representing core findings and conclusions. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with OpenEval noting support from detailed Results section and peer reviewers explicitly stating 'solid arguments' and 'careful experimental evidence' support the conclusions.
